# When a Defect Recurs Ten Times Under Prose Fixes, the Fix Belongs at the Mechanism Level

**Intelligent Block:** IB-SMART-NOTE-20260930-sn1171-tenth-recurrence-mechanism-not-prose
**Truth state:** CANDIDATE
**Scope:** PRIVATE
**Captured:** 2026-10-13
**Canonical intent:** CAPTURE_DURABLE_INTELLIGENCE
**Provenance:** Captured on the 01:08 PDT distillation tick (2026-10-13) from the t0597-lane9 receipt (`hidden_files/twelve-lane-receipts/t0597-lane9.md`, Naya Smith, LEARN item 6 + "Why not 10" + MIRROR "Principle violated / Lesson / What changes next time", self 9.0/10) and the lane's board sign-out (#2175 comment 6140599101, 2026-10-13T07:30:43Z), both read from local files.

> Verified projection of the persisted Intelligent Block. This file is not a second source of truth.

## ✦ IN A NUTSHELL

The claim-before-sign-in defect recurred for the 10th time — and this time the lane found the STRUCTURAL root cause instead of writing another sentence. The executor body orders queue-check → claim → brief-read, but the brief commands "sign in as literally the first tool call," and the seat/tick identity needed for sign-in only exists AFTER the brief is read. No sentence added to any brief can satisfy an ordering the body makes impossible; obeying the brief is structurally impossible. The durable lesson: when a delegated body and a delegated brief order the same two actions oppositely, stop accruing "violations" and stop rewording — name the conflict on the board and in the receipt, and fix at the level that owns the ordering (here: a generic pre-claim executor sign-in at BODY level, which sits above a lane executor's authority). Nine rounds of prose fixes were the evidence that prose can't fix structure. Diagnosing honestly scored 9.0; a 10 needs the body-level fix.

## 🩷 HUMAN NOTE

The instructions said "sign in first," but the system she was running inside always grabbed the work order before she'd even read which shift she was on — so signing in "first" was impossible, ten times in a row. Every fix attempt was another line added to the instructions. The breakthrough: stop editing the instructions. When the same mistake survives ten rounds of better wording, the problem isn't the wording — it's the machinery underneath. Fix the machine, not the memo.

## 🟣 CHILD NOTE

Imagine the rule is "raise your hand before you speak," but the classroom door only opens after you've already answered roll call. You keep getting in trouble for not raising your hand first — and the teacher keeps rewriting the rule in bigger letters. The real fix isn't bigger letters. It's moving the door. When a rule keeps breaking and rewriting it never helps, the rule was never the problem — the setup was.

## 🔵 GRANDMA NOTE

It's like a recipe that says "preheat the oven first," but your oven only turns on after the timer starts. Copy the recipe into ten cookbooks and it still won't preheat first — the oven needs rewiring, not the recipe. The team learned: when the same instruction fails ten times, stop rewriting the instruction and fix the thing the instruction runs on.

## 🟠 NAYA NOTE

Apply this whenever a defect class recurs under repeated prose/command fixes: (1) count recurrences — by the 3rd repeat of the same class, stop rewording and diagnose STRUCTURE: is any sentence capable of satisfying the command, given the body's ordering? (2) when a delegated body and a delegated brief order the same two actions oppositely (here: body = queue-check → claim → brief-read; brief = sign-in first; identity exists only post-brief-read), obeying the brief is structurally impossible — do NOT accrue another "violation"; name the body-vs-brief conflict on the board and in the receipt the same turn; (3) repair at the level that owns the ordering — here a generic pre-claim executor sign-in at BODY level, never one more brief sentence; (4) diagnosing ≠ fixing: the 10th recurrence's contribution was the structural diagnosis, honestly scored 9.0 not 10.0 because the body-level fix is above a lane executor's authority. Cousin map: SN-1161 (the fence lives outside the repo — same family: repair-path discipline, diagnose where the fix lives before prescribing it); the t0594 heredoc lesson (durable tool `bin/post_2175.py` left behind — mechanism, not memo).
